deep.reconstruction:
The page holds three independent algebraic scratch calculations.

(A) Top left and middle left: Cramer's rule / Lagrange interpolation for a quadratic.
Riemann writes the 3x4 array
  [1, α, α², a]
  [1, β, β², b]
  [1, γ, γ², c]
and expands its 3x3 minors.
- The minor on the first three columns is the Vandermonde determinant: p = βγ² + αβ² + α²γ − γβ² − α²β − αγ² = (β−α)(γ−α)(γ−β).
- A minor containing the last column, s = βc + αb + aγ − bγ − aβ − αc = det[[1,α,a],[1,β,b],[1,γ,c]].
- Further six-term expansions labelled r, q and a second s. They are partly illegible. By the obvious pattern (my reading) they are the remaining minors, e.g. det[[1,α²,a],...] and det[[α,α²,a],...].
By Cramer's rule these minors are, up to sign and division by p, the coefficients of the unique quadratic P(y) = A + By + Cy² with P(α)=a, P(β)=b, P(γ)=c.

The main formula of this block writes P in Lagrange form:
  z = [x + a(y−β)(y−γ)/((α−β)(α−γ)) + b(y−α)(y−γ)/((β−α)(β−γ)) + c(y−α)(y−β)/((γ−α)(γ−β))] / ((y−α)(y−β)(y−γ)),
that is, z = (x + P(y))/((y−α)(y−β)(y−γ)).

My interpretation (not stated on the page): x is an algebraic function of y, e.g. x² = f(y) with (α,a), (β,b), (γ,c) points on the curve. Then x + P(y) vanishes at the points (α,−a), (β,−b), (γ,−c). So z is a rational function on the curve whose finite poles are restricted to (α,a), (β,b), (γ,c). This is the kind of construction used for addition and inversion on hyperelliptic curves. An earlier attempt z = x/((y−α)(y−β)(y−γ)) is struck through.

(B) Top right: Plücker coordinates of a line.
- The two rows K1..K4 and K1'..K4' define the 2x2 minors (ij) = K_iK_j' − K_jK_i'. The ratio (K1'K2 − K2'K1)/(K1K3 − K3'K1) is one such quotient.
- Riemann writes the quadratic Plücker relation 13·24 + 14·32 + 12·43 = 0.
- He normalises 13 = 24 and sets a = 14/13, b = 32/13, c = 12/13.
- Dividing the relation by 13² gives 24/13 + ab + c·43/13 = 0, hence 43/13 = −(1+ab)/c.
- Then 43/12 = (43/13)/(12/13) = −(1+ab)/c².
- Also 14/32 = a/b.
So the line is parametrised by three affine parameters a, b, c.

(C) Bottom half: Jacobi inversion for genus 2 (hyperelliptic integrals, x_i² = f(y_i)).
The two integrals are
  du = dy1/x1 + dy2/x2,  dv = y1dy1/x1 + y2dy2/x2.
The transcription reads the dv line as y2dy1/x1 + y1dy2/x2; the final results require y1dy1/x1 + y2dy2/x2.

The symmetric functions are a = y1 + y2 and b = y1y2. Then da = dy1 + dy2 and db = y2dy1 + y1dy2.

Solving for dy1, dy2 (correct form):
  (y1−y2)dy1 = y1da − db,  (y2−y1)dy2 = y2da − db.
Substituting:
  du = [(y1x2 − y2x1)da − (x2−x1)db] / ((y1−y2)x1x2)
  dv = [(y1²x2 − y2²x1)da − (y1x2 − y2x1)db] / ((y1−y2)x1x2).

Riemann then forms the functional determinant. He expands (y1x2 − y2x1)(y2x2 − y1x1) − (x2−x1)²y1y2 as y1y2(x1²+x2²) − x1x2(y1²+y2²) − y1y2(x1−x2)² = −x1x2(y1−y2)². This gives ∂(u,v)/∂(a,b) = −1/(x1x2), equivalently ∂(a,b)/∂(u,v) = −x1x2.

Finally he inverts directly:
  (y2−y1)dy1/x1 = y2du − dv,  (y1−y2)dy2/x2 = y1du − dv.
This yields
  ∂y1/∂u = y2x1/(y2−y1),  ∂y1/∂v = −x1/(y2−y1),
  ∂y2/∂u = y1x2/(y1−y2),  ∂y2/∂v = −x2/(y1−y2),
  ∂y1/∂v = −(1/y2)∂y1/∂u, and similarly for y2.
He also has partly illegible expressions for ∂x_i/∂u and ∂x_i/∂v. Via x_i² = f(y_i) these should be ∂x1/∂u = f'(y1)y2/(2(y2−y1)), etc.

These are the derivatives of the inverse functions of a genus-2 hyperelliptic integral pair, the standard starting point for expressing y1+y2 and y1y2 as abelian (theta-quotient) functions of (u,v).

The page has no explicit link to the neighbouring pages (a ±1 count table before, elasticity of a bent body after).
errors: Elimination step: with b = y1y2 (db = y2dy1 + y1dy2), the correct relations are (y1−y2)dy1 = y1da − db and (y2−y1)dy2 = y2da − db. The page (as transcribed) writes y2da − db = (y2−y1)dy1 and y1da − db = (y1−y2)dy2, with the multipliers swapped. That version would correspond to db = y1dy1 + y2dy2. It may be a slip or a misreading.
The denominator of du is written (y2−y1)x2x1; the correct one, given the numerator (y1x2 − x1y2)da − (x2−x1)db, is (y1−y2)x1x2. This is a sign slip, possibly in the transcription.

The dv line is transcribed as y2dy1/x1 + y1dy2/x2. That differential is not exact (∂(y2/x1)/∂y2 = 1/x1 ≠ 1/x2 = ∂(y1/x2)/∂y1). Riemann's final partial derivatives require dv = y1dy1/x1 + y2dy2/x2. Most likely this is a transcription misreading; otherwise it is a slip on the page.

The intermediate dv numerator (x2−x1)y2y1da − (y1x1−y2x2)db does not match the dv of the standard pair; signs and terms are inconsistent. The final determinant −x1x2(y1−y2)² and the inverse derivatives are nonetheless correct.
The expressions for ∂x1/∂u and ∂x2/∂u are illegible or garbled in the transcription ('x y1y2/(y2−y1)'); they cannot be verified as written.

results.what: Vandermonde determinant and the 3x3 minors of [1, α_i, α_i², a_i]: coefficients of the interpolating quadratic via Cramer's rule
results.modern_name: Vandermonde determinant / Cramer's rule for polynomial interpolation

results.what: z = (x + P(y))/((y−α)(y−β)(y−γ)) with P the Lagrange interpolant through (α,a), (β,b), (γ,c): a function on the curve with prescribed poles
results.modern_name: Lagrange interpolation; construction of rational functions on a hyperelliptic curve (addition / inversion problem)
results.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (1795); the hyperelliptic use goes back to Abel and Jacobi

results.what: 13·24 + 14·32 + 12·43 = 0 for the 2x2 minors of a 2x4 matrix, and its affine normalisation 43/13 = −(1+ab)/c
results.modern_name: Quadratic Plücker relation for line coordinates (Grassmannian G(2,4))
results.usually_credited_to: Plücker (1865–68) for line geometry; the determinant identity itself goes back to Cayley (1859, 'six coordinates of a line'), and the Grassmann/Sylvester tradition

results.what: Inversion of du = Σdy_i/x_i, dv = Σy_idy_i/x_i: explicit ∂y_i/∂u, ∂y_i/∂v and Jacobian ∂(y1+y2, y1y2)/∂(u,v) = −x1x2
results.modern_name: Jacobi inversion problem for genus 2; differential equations of the hyperelliptic abelian functions

deep.surprise_reason: Everything here is standard 19th-century algebra: Vandermonde/Cramer, Lagrange interpolation, the Plücker relation for a 2x4 matrix, and the Jacobi–Göpel–Rosenhain inversion differentials for genus 2. All of it fits Riemann's known work on abelian functions around 1853–57. The Plücker-type identity predates Plücker's line geometry only as a determinant identity, which was already known (Cayley 1859, and earlier). Nothing goes beyond routine scratch work.

checkable.sympy: al,be,ga,a,b,c=symbols('alpha beta gamma a b c'); simplify(Matrix([[1,al,a],[1,be,b],[1,ga,c]]).det() - (be*c+al*b+a*ga-b*ga-a*be-al*c))
checkable.asserts: the expansion s of the minor with columns (1, α, a) is correct (result 0)

checkable.sympy: al,be,ga,a,b,c,y=symbols('alpha beta gamma a b c y'); P=a*(y-be)*(y-ga)/((al-be)*(al-ga))+b*(y-al)*(y-ga)/((be-al)*(be-ga))+c*(y-al)*(y-be)/((ga-al)*(ga-be)); [simplify(P.subs(y,al)-a),simplify(P.subs(y,be)-b),simplify(P.subs(y,ga)-c)]
checkable.asserts: the numerator polynomial interpolates a, b, c at α, β, γ (results [0,0,0])

transcription_corrections: The top-left minor is probably 'βc + αb + aγ − bγ − aβ − αc' (Greek α in the second term), i.e. det[[1,α,a],[1,β,b],[1,γ,c]].
The Vandermonde line should read 'βγ² + αβ² + α²γ − γβ² − α²β − αγ² = p'; the transcription has '−αβ' for '−α²β'.
In 'dv = ...' the integrand is likely y1dy1/x1 + y2dy2/x2, not y2dy1/x1 + y1dy2/x2; the final derivatives require the former.
'(K1'K2 − K2'K1)/(K1K3 − K3'K)': the last factor is K1, i.e. K1K3' − K3K1' type minors (primes uncertain).
'(y2−y1)dy1 = y2da − dv' should be '(y2−y1)dy1/x1 = y2du − dv' (du, with division by x1), matching the companion line '(y1−y2)dy2/x2 = y1du − dv'.
The struck '∂y/∂v = ∂a/∂u' fragment and the 'x y1y2/(y2−y1)' for ∂x1/∂u are unreliable readings.
The last bottom-right entry is probably '∂y2/∂v = −x2/(y1−y2)' rather than '∂x2/∂v = −y2/(y1−y2)'.
